title: THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE
text:
rather than their feet. Those letters I have sent on to the secretary, Mrs. J. B. May, editor of the "Savoy Star," for she will know how to handle them. If she is off the press you will find out how much they all think of you boys and the love. Little (my wife) I can recall ever taking an active part in a love—just stood around and watched others. Little (my wife) may not agree with me but I can recall that the night she was going out with the boys a long time before I quit going barefooted. I went barefooted so long waiting, playing first base, that I made it through those old outfield shoes by stepping on a groundball while knowing a woman was watching, and then spiked my feet so that other boys just couldn't follow me. I would rest up and come right back. You may also notice that some of the mothers of these same love boys had their tongues hanging out.

Gus says you are busy but too old to furnish the music, but I think at least you could manage the affair, and give your personal touch to help us get up a show even though it doesn't make music. You know it is a comedy act in which I played the role of a bashful country cousin in which you and Barry acted the part of the fresh city cousin, and as the script called for it you were given a scheme to exploit me and I recall that when the young lady in question heard of way said that I wouldn't let her do it even though she wanted to. Our problem seems to be to round up the actors, put in a night or so doing something less than a dance, and make as though they believe it was really worth while. Take it calmly old boy and have.

Please write the "Savoy Star" what you boys think about it. Is it right enough? Do you think a dance on the 13th instant may comment on your attitude."

Affectionately,*

My wife good read my letter of yesterday after it was that Mrs. Montgomery "suggested that we have a meeting, drawing on ourselves." The plans were so far advanced at that time that you could hardly push anything farther than committee business, without even the boys being too embarrassed in order to be pleased. The idea of a possible banquet was far from it.

*Letter to Messrs. Barry and Bob Taylor from Mr. E. A. McMahon, Dallas, Texas, December 1, 1937.
notes: Printed page number 191 appears at top right. Title 'THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE' appears at top left. Footnote marker (*) references letter from E. A. McMahon to Barry and Bob Taylor, Dallas, Texas, December 1, 1937.
